metadata.title: Seed Domain: Math And Abstraction Roots
metadata.description: Machine-parseable seed graph for early math and abstraction relation motifs. This is a first executable abstraction scaffold, not a formal mathematics ontology.
notes: This graph uses the 66 first-set math-abstraction situations, not all 117 high-priority rows.
Formal algebra, proof, probability, and institutional measurement are intentionally excluded from this first seed.
Math concepts are represented as abstractions built from reusable relation schemas, not as primitives.

layers.label: Math Observation Channels
layers.description: Observable inputs such as visual attribute, touch counting, speech number, symbol mark, spatial layout, pattern sequence, and rule instruction.

layers.label: Math Relational Invariants
layers.description: Reusable comparison, quantity, correspondence, order, grouping, spatial, part-whole, repetition, and condition relations.

layers.label: Math Schemas
layers.description: Reusable abstraction-building patterns such as matching, counting, comparing, sorting, measuring, patterning, symbol mapping, and rule transfer.

layers.label: Math Symbols
layers.description: Symbol handles such as number words, written numbers, tally marks, and simple chart marks.

layers.label: Math Objects And Handles
layers.description: Concrete handles used in early abstraction tasks: items, sets, containers, paths, measuring units, attributes, and rules.

layers.label: Math Event Outcomes
layers.description: Reusable outcomes such as match found, count error, quantity change, leftover, order followed, rule applied, prediction, and transfer.

layers.label: Math Abstractions
layers.description: Early abstractions built from relation patterns: number, quantity, order, grouping, measurement, pattern, symbolic representation, logic, and abstraction.

nodes.label: visual attribute observation
nodes.summary: Source for color, shape, size, position, sameness, and visible difference.

nodes.label: touch counting observation
nodes.summary: Source for pointing, touching, handing out, pairing, and repeated unit placement.

nodes.label: speech number observation
nodes.summary: Source for spoken number words and ordered counting tokens.

nodes.label: symbol and mark observation
nodes.summary: Source for written numerals, tally marks, chart bars, arrows, and labels.

nodes.label: spatial layout observation
nodes.summary: Source for inside, outside, on, under, path, blockage, fit, and alignment.

nodes.label: sequence and pattern observation
nodes.summary: Source for before/after, ordered steps, repeated cycles, rhythms, and missing elements.

nodes.label: rule instruction observation
nodes.summary: Source for if/then, not, and, or, and reusable rule instructions.

nodes.label: quantity estimate observation
nodes.summary: Source for more, less, equal, full, half-full, heavy, light, and approximate amount.

nodes.label: same/different
nodes.summary: Compares whether items, attributes, symbols, or outcomes match or differ.

nodes.label: zero/one/many
nodes.summary: Distinguishes none, one, two, and many as reusable quantity states.

nodes.label: more/less/equal
nodes.summary: Compares amount, count, length, level, weight, and distribution.

nodes.label: one-to-one
nodes.summary: Pairs one source item with one target item without duplication or omission.

nodes.label: before/after
nodes.summary: Orders states, count tokens, steps, and events in time.

nodes.label: order position
nodes.summary: Tracks first, last, next, previous, increasing order, and decreasing order.

nodes.label: group/member
nodes.summary: Tracks whether an item belongs inside or outside a rule-defined group.

nodes.label: property presence/absence
nodes.summary: Tracks whether a selected property is present, absent, negated, or required.

nodes.label: inside/outside
nodes.summary: Tracks containment and non-containment as a portable spatial abstraction.

nodes.label: on/under
nodes.summary: Tracks on-top and under positions as contrastable spatial relations.

nodes.label: path blocked/unblocked
nodes.summary: Tracks whether movement through a path can continue or is stopped.

nodes.label: part/whole
nodes.summary: Tracks how parts combine into wholes or fail to complete a whole.

nodes.label: repeats
nodes.summary: Tracks repeated structures, cycles, rhythms, and expected next elements.

nodes.label: expected/unexpected
nodes.summary: Tracks whether a count, order, pattern, measurement, or rule application matches expectation.

nodes.label: condition/action
nodes.summary: Tracks a condition that selects, permits, blocks, or triggers an action.

nodes.label: attribute match
nodes.summary: Items are treated as matching when a selected attribute is the same.

nodes.label: attribute contrast
nodes.summary: Items are treated as different when a selected attribute differs.

nodes.label: odd one out
nodes.summary: One item fails the shared relation that holds for the rest of a small group.

nodes.label: match selection
nodes.summary: A matching item is selected from alternatives using a target attribute relation.

nodes.label: object count
nodes.summary: Distinct visible items are represented as a quantity state.

nodes.label: counting correspondence
nodes.summary: Each distinct item receives one counting action and one ordered count token.

nodes.label: double count error
nodes.summary: The same item is counted more than once.

nodes.label: skip count error
nodes.summary: A distinct item is not counted.

nodes.label: add-one quantity change
nodes.summary: Adding one item changes the quantity upward.

nodes.label: remove-one quantity change
nodes.summary: Removing one item changes the quantity downward.

nodes.label: quantity comparison
nodes.summary: Two sets or amounts are compared as more, less, or equal.

nodes.label: one-to-one assignment
nodes.summary: One item is assigned to each target member.

nodes.label: pairing correspondence
nodes.summary: Items are matched in pairs using a compatible target relation.

nodes.label: unmatched leftover
nodes.summary: An item remains after attempted one-to-one assignment or pairing.

nodes.label: unequal distribution
nodes.summary: Targets receive unequal counts or amounts.

nodes.label: extra item
nodes.summary: One target or set has an additional item relative to another.

nodes.label: ordered series
nodes.summary: Items are arranged by increasing value along a selected dimension.

nodes.label: reverse order
nodes.summary: Items are arranged by decreasing value along the same dimension.

nodes.label: ordinal position
nodes.summary: An item is located at a position such as first, last, next, or previous.

nodes.label: event sequence order
nodes.summary: Events are arranged in a before/after order.

nodes.label: instruction step order
nodes.summary: A multi-step instruction is represented as an ordered action sequence.

nodes.label: order violation
nodes.summary: An expected order is swapped, skipped, or otherwise violated.

nodes.label: property grouping
nodes.summary: Items are grouped because they share a selected property.

nodes.label: category grouping
nodes.summary: Items are grouped by object kind or category.

nodes.label: function grouping
nodes.summary: Items are grouped by what they can do or how they are used.

nodes.label: multi-attribute filter
nodes.summary: Selection depends on more than one property or relation.

nodes.label: sorting rule
nodes.summary: A rule determines which group each item belongs to.

nodes.label: rule change
nodes.summary: The active sorting or selection rule changes, requiring reclassification.

nodes.label: negated property filter
nodes.summary: Items are selected because they do not have a property.

nodes.label: containment fit
nodes.summary: An object fits inside a container boundary.

nodes.label: fit failure
nodes.summary: An object cannot fit inside a boundary and must remain outside or beside it.

nodes.label: spatial position relation
nodes.summary: A position relation such as on, under, beside, or between is represented explicitly.

nodes.label: path following
nodes.summary: A route is followed through ordered movement markers.

nodes.label: path blockage
nodes.summary: A route cannot be completed because an obstacle blocks continuation.

nodes.label: shape composition
nodes.summary: Parts combine to produce a whole shape.

nodes.label: level comparison
nodes.summary: Visible levels such as full and half-full are compared.

nodes.label: quantity conservation candidate
nodes.summary: The same amount may remain despite a changed container shape or visual appearance.

nodes.label: aligned measurement comparison
nodes.summary: Lengths are compared by aligning starting points.

nodes.label: repeated unit measurement
nodes.summary: A stable unit is reused to measure a length or extent.

nodes.label: measurement gap error
nodes.summary: Gaps or overlaps between repeated units make the measurement unreliable.

nodes.label: cross-property independence
nodes.summary: One property such as size does not determine another property such as weight.

nodes.label: alternating pattern
nodes.summary: A sequence repeats by alternating elements.

nodes.label: cyclic pattern
nodes.summary: A sequence repeats as a cycle with more than two elements.

nodes.label: rhythm pattern
nodes.summary: A sound or action sequence repeats in time.

nodes.label: missing pattern element
nodes.summary: A missing element is inferred from the surrounding repeated pattern.

nodes.label: next item prediction
nodes.summary: The next item is predicted from a repeated relation structure.

nodes.label: number symbol binding
nodes.summary: A spoken number and written numeral are bound as handles for the same quantity relation.

nodes.label: quantity symbol mapping
nodes.summary: A visible quantity such as dots is mapped to a number symbol.

nodes.label: tally event count
nodes.summary: A mark is added for each event or item to preserve a count record.

nodes.label: category count display
nodes.summary: Categories are displayed with visible quantities.

nodes.label: bar length quantity display
nodes.summary: Bar length or height represents relative quantity.

nodes.label: conditional action rule
nodes.summary: A condition selects or triggers an action.

nodes.label: signal conditioned action
nodes.summary: A signal state determines the action to perform.

nodes.label: not filter
nodes.summary: A property is excluded from the selected set.

nodes.label: and filter
nodes.summary: Selection requires two or more conditions to be true.

nodes.label: or filter
nodes.summary: Selection accepts any one of multiple conditions.

nodes.label: rule transfer
nodes.summary: The same rule is applied to a new set of objects.

nodes.label: number word
nodes.summary: Spoken handle such as one, two, or three.

nodes.label: written number
nodes.summary: Written numeral such as 3.

nodes.label: tally mark
nodes.summary: One mark used to record one event or item.

nodes.label: chart bar
nodes.summary: Visible bar whose length or height represents quantity.

nodes.label: item
nodes.summary: Generic countable item such as a biscuit, toy, cup, bead, or block.

nodes.label: set
nodes.summary: A group of items treated together.

nodes.label: attribute
nodes.summary: Selected property such as color, shape, size, function, or texture.

nodes.label: container
nodes.summary: Box, cup, glass, basket, or other boundary for containment and fit.

nodes.label: path
nodes.summary: Route or ordered movement path.

nodes.label: measure unit
nodes.summary: Reusable unit such as a hand span or block.

nodes.label: rule
nodes.summary: Condition or selection pattern that can be applied to items.

nodes.label: match found
nodes.summary: A selected item matches the target relation.

nodes.label: counting error
nodes.summary: A count is unreliable because of duplication or omission.

nodes.label: quantity increase
nodes.summary: Quantity rises after an addition.

nodes.label: quantity decrease
nodes.summary: Quantity falls after a removal.

nodes.label: leftover detected
nodes.summary: An unmatched item remains after attempted pairing or distribution.

nodes.label: order followed
nodes.summary: Items, events, or instructions follow the expected order.

nodes.label: prediction success
nodes.summary: A repeated relation supports the expected next item or action.

nodes.label: rule applied
nodes.summary: A rule is used to select, sort, or act.

nodes.label: relation transfer
nodes.summary: The same relation structure is applied to new objects.

nodes.label: number
nodes.summary: Stable abstraction built from countable items, count words, symbols, and correspondence.

nodes.label: quantity
nodes.summary: Amount or count represented through comparison, change, and equality.

nodes.label: order
nodes.summary: Arrangement by sequence, position, before/after, or increasing/decreasing dimension.

nodes.label: grouping
nodes.summary: Collection membership determined by a selected property, category, function, or rule.

nodes.label: measurement
nodes.summary: Comparison using alignment, levels, stable repeated units, and error checks.

nodes.label: pattern
nodes.summary: Repeated relation structure that supports completion and prediction.

nodes.label: symbolic representation
nodes.summary: A mark, word, numeral, or display stands for quantity or relation structure.

nodes.label: logical rule
nodes.summary: Condition, negation, conjunction, disjunction, or rule over objects.

nodes.label: abstraction
nodes.summary: Reusable relation structure applied across different objects or situations.

micro_experiences.title: Same, different, match, and odd one out
events: two identical red blocks are shown
a red block and a blue block are shown
a matching sock is selected
one odd sock is found in a matching set
language_overlay: Two things can match on one attribute, and one item can be different from the group.

micro_experiences.title: Counting items, double count, and skip count
events: one biscuit is placed on a plate
two biscuits are placed on a plate
a child points to each toy while number words are spoken
the same toy is counted twice
one toy is skipped
language_overlay: Counting works when each item is counted once; counting the same item twice or skipping an item creates an error.

micro_experiences.title: More, equal, one-to-one, and leftover
events: one bowl has more grapes than another
two bowls have the same number of grapes
one cup is given to each person
one shoe is left after pairs are made
language_overlay: Amounts can be compared, and one-to-one assignment can reveal a leftover.

micro_experiences.title: Ordering items and following steps
events: blocks are arranged from smallest to largest
blocks are arranged from largest to smallest
picture cards are placed in routine order
a two-step instruction is swapped
a three-step instruction is followed in order
language_overlay: Order can be increasing, decreasing, temporal, or instruction-based.

micro_experiences.title: Grouping by property and changing the rule
events: red objects are put in one basket
round objects are put in one basket
red round objects and red square objects are separated
the sorting rule changes halfway
not-red items are selected
language_overlay: A group is made by a rule, and changing the rule changes group membership.

micro_experiences.title: Fit, position, and path blockage
events: a small toy fits inside a box
a large toy does not fit inside the box
a ball is placed under a chair
a ball is placed on top of a chair
a path is followed until it is blocked
language_overlay: Spatial relations such as inside, on, under, and blocked path can be reused as abstract structure.

micro_experiences.title: Parts, level, alignment, and measurement errors
events: two half-circles are joined into a circle
a full glass and half-full glass are compared
two ropes are lined up from the same end
a block is reused to measure a shelf
gaps are left between measuring blocks
language_overlay: Measurement depends on alignment, stable units, and no gaps or overlaps.

micro_experiences.title: Patterns, symbols, tallies, and charts
events: beads repeat red and blue
a missing bead is inferred
the next story picture is predicted
spoken three and written 3 are linked
tally marks record children entering
a bar chart shows favorite fruits
language_overlay: A symbol or repeated pattern points to relation structure, not just to a visual mark.

micro_experiences.title: If, not, and, or, and rule transfer
events: if shoes are wet they stay outside
if the light is red the child stops
a snack that is not spicy is selected
a toy that is red and soft is selected
a toy that is red or soft is selected
the same rule is used on a new set
language_overlay: A rule can select, block, combine, or transfer across new objects.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can two blocks match in shape while still differing in color?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Matching depends on the selected attribute. Same/different must be evaluated relative to color, shape, size, or another chosen property.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is touching the same toy twice while counting different from touching each toy once?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Counting needs one-to-one correspondence between distinct items and count tokens. Touching the same item twice breaks that correspondence.

evaluation_questions.question: What relation changes when one more toy is added to a row?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The before/after quantity state changes upward by one, causing a quantity increase.

evaluation_questions.question: Why does one shoe left after pairing show that the pairing was incomplete?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: One-to-one pairing tries to match each item with a compatible target. A leftover item means a corresponding pair was not found.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can swapping two steps change whether an instruction was followed correctly?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The instruction is an ordered sequence. Swapping steps violates the expected order even if both actions happen.

evaluation_questions.question: Why does changing the sorting rule change which basket an item belongs in?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Group membership is determined by the active rule. When the rule changes, the same item may need to be classified differently.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is a large toy beside a box different from a small toy inside the box?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Both use containment, but the large toy fails the fit relation and remains outside or beside the container.

evaluation_questions.question: Why do gaps between measuring blocks make a shelf measurement unreliable?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Repeated-unit measurement requires stable units placed continuously. Gaps violate the measurement relation.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can a child predict the next bead in a red-blue-red-blue pattern?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The sequence repeats. The repeated relation structure supports next-item prediction.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can written 3 stand for three dots?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The written number is a symbol bound to a quantity relation. It is a handle for the count, not the count itself.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is using the same sorting rule on a new set an abstraction?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The object set changes, but the relation rule remains reusable. The same relation structure transfers across objects.
